description: Create a new FiGuard budget for an agent session. Returns a session_token that must be passed to figuard_authorize. The session_token is only returned once — store it for the duration of the agent session. Use currency (e.g. 'USD') for monetary budgets. Use unit (e.g. 'tokens') for resource budgets. Optionally add allocations to ring-fence spend by category (e.g. separate limits for flights and hotels). Pass external_reference to make this call idempotent: if a live budget with that reference already exists it is returned (HTTP 200) instead of creating a duplicate. If the reference exists but with a different configuration, a 409 is returned. Use this to safely handle orchestrator restarts.

allocations.description: Optional category-level caps. Each allocation is an independent maximum — flights capped at $300 means flights can never exceed $300, regardless of what other categories spend. Allocation limits must not exceed total_limit but do not need to sum to it — the remainder is a shared pool. Example: total_limit=1000, allocations=[{flights: 500}, {hotels: 200}] — valid, $300 remains as unallocated headroom.

allowed_categories.description: Required when enforcement_mode is CATEGORY_CONSTRAINED or STRICT. Omit for OPEN mode. Defines which claimedCategory values this allocation will accept. Example: ["flight"] for a flights allocation.

enforcement_mode.description: STRICT blocks any claimed_item_type in forbidden_item_types. CATEGORY_CONSTRAINED checks claimed_category. OPEN allows anything within the limit.

forbidden_item_types.description: Specific item types to block (e.g. 'gift_card', 'upgrade'). Only applies in STRICT mode.

anomaly_detection_enabled.description: When true, FiGuard monitors spend requests for statistical anomalies. Recommended for production.

auto_pause_on_anomaly.description: Controls anomaly response mode. When true (default), an anomalous request pauses the budget — no further spend until a human resumes it. When false (advisory mode), the anomalous request is still denied and ANOMALY_DETECTED webhook fires, but the budget stays ACTIVE. Use false for high-throughput agents where a single spike should not halt the entire fleet.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR'). Required for monetary budgets. Omit for resource budgets.

expires_in.description: How long the budget is valid. Accepts '24h', '7d', '30m', or a number of seconds. Defaults to '24h'.

external_reference.description: Optional stable identifier for this budget (e.g. 'run-abc-123', 'order-456'). When provided, re-calling figuard_create_budget with the same external_reference returns the existing live budget instead of creating a duplicate — safe for orchestrator restarts.

intent_context.description: Optional human-readable description of what this budget is for (e.g. 'Book travel to NYC for user_123').

total_limit.description: Maximum total amount the agent is allowed to spend. For USD budgets this is dollars, not cents.

unit.description: Resource unit label (e.g. 'tokens', 'api_calls'). Required for resource budgets. Omit for monetary budgets.

user_id.description: Identifier for the user or agent session this budget belongs to.

velocity_max_amount_per_hour.description: Max total requestedQuantity per rolling 1-hour window.

velocity_max_per_day.description: Max authorize attempts per rolling 24-hour window.

velocity_max_per_minute.description: Max authorize attempts per rolling 1-minute window. Denied with VELOCITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when exceeded.

name: figuard_create_budget
